0.long_answer: Nephroblastoma, more commonly known as Wilms tumor, is named after the German surgeon Carl Max Wilhelm Wilms (1867–1918), who is credited with its initial description. His detailed examination of the tumor in the 19th century laid the groundwork for understanding this pediatric renal cancer, and his name has since been permanently associated with the condition in medical literature.

1.long_answer: The surgeon in question, Carl Max Wilhelm Wilms, earned his medical doctorate in 1890 from the University of Bonn. This year marks the completion of his medical education before he started his professional training and surgical career.
